title: Zendesk Jira Integration: How to Set It Up (2026)
summary: Zendesk Jira integration can be set up in 15 minutes with the official app. Decide whether its features cover your needs.
body_markdown:
## Install and connect the integration in five steps


Once your plan allows Marketplace apps, the install is five steps done in order, and each one leaves something you can check before moving on. Skip the check and you find the break three steps later, in a ticket sidebar that shows nothing.


Take the sequence below as the order that keeps each failure traceable to one step. It runs from the Jira install to a synced comment.


### Step 1: Install the Jira side


Sign in to Jira as a site administrator, open the Atlassian Marketplace from the Apps menu, and search for Zendesk Support for Jira. Select it, choose Get app, and accept the prompts.


A non-admin account won't see the install option, so find the right login before you book anyone's time.


Check: the app appears under Manage apps. Take a screenshot of that list showing the app enabled.


### Step 2: Add the Zendesk side in Admin Center


In Zendesk, open Admin Center and go to Apps and integrations, then Integrations. Find the Jira entry and choose to add it. You need admin rights in Zendesk too. This step creates the Zendesk half of the connection but doesn't yet point it anywhere.


Check: Jira now appears as an integration in Admin Center, with no connected site. Capture this screen, because the empty state is what you compare against after Step 3.


### Step 3: Link the two with the Jira URL and permissions


Enter your Jira site address in the URL field, then select the connect option. Jira opens a consent screen listing what Zendesk may read and write.


Read it before approving, since this is where a security reviewer will ask questions, and approve it with the Jira account you want the link to run under.


That account matters. The link attributes every issue and comment it creates to that account, so a personal login means a colleague's name on every ticket-driven issue after they leave. Use a dedicated account if your policy allows one.


Check: the integration page shows your Jira site as connected. Screenshot the Jira app configuration alongside it.


### Create and link your first Jira issue


Open any ticket and find the Jira section in the ticket sidebar. Choose to create an issue, pick the project and issue type, complete the required fields, and submit.


If a field your Jira project requires is missing from the form, creation fails, so fix that in Jira's project settings rather than guessing.


Check: the issue key appears in the sidebar and the ticket shows as linked inside Jira. Screenshot the sidebar.


### Turn on Zendesk Jira comment and status sync


Return to the integration settings and enable sync for comments and status. Then test both directions: add a comment on the Jira issue, and confirm it reaches the ticket, then change the issue's status and watch for the update.


With a working, synced pair in place, the next question is what this setup refuses to do.
